title: an UNANNOTATED function containing panic(...) infers a plain return type, so no Result recovery surface exists to swallow the panic
notes: specification/failures.mdx §Panic Does Not Widen a Return Type: 'Calling `panic(...)` MUST NOT force a function's return type to widen into `Result<A, Panic>`.' and 'A function that validates an argument, refuses a forgery, or asserts an invariant MUST therefore be able to abort with `panic(...)` while keeping a plain return type.' docs/DECISIONS.md carries the matching Locked entry ('Calling `panic(...)` does not widen a return type into `Result<A, Panic>` … the prohibition is on the compiler forcing it'). `E` is the expected-error channel (reference/function-channels.mdx) and a panic is not an expected error, so a construct that aborts with `panic(...)` keeps whatever return type it declares. The inference half of the rule, and the half that was proved broken by EXECUTION rather than by reading a diagnostic. docs/DECISIONS.md (Locked): 'An unannotated function that reaches `throw error`, propagates an error Result with `!`, or returns a Result is inferred as Result<A, E>' — `panic(...)` is none of those three, and specification/failures.mdx §Panic Does Not Widen a Return Type says the compiler may not force the widening. Before the rule landed this function inferred Result<string, Panic>, and the same program with `.unwrapOr("fallback")` in place of the Result.try boundary compiled with ZERO diagnostics and printed "fallback": the panic was consumed as an ordinary failure and vanished from the caller's row. A diagnostics-only case would not have caught that, because there were no diagnostics to declare. This case is written as `output` for that reason and both of its lines execute. Line 1 also fails against the pre-rule tree for a second, independent reason: an inferred Result placed into a `string[]` literal is an unconsumed Result.
